summary: Search ascending with find, visiting every integer index in the snapshotted range including holes.

target.notes: Snapshot length, then for every index in range perform Get rather than HasProperty; absent elements therefore produce undefined and still invoke the predicate. Invoke through JsFunction.Call and apply JsValue.IsTruthy. Stop at the first truthy predicate result.

semantics.callback_this: thisArg or undefined via canonical call semantics
semantics.callback_callable_check: TypeError before iteration if callback is not callable

caveats: Unlike map/filter/some/every/forEach/reduce, the find family does not skip empty slots; predicates run for them with undefined.
Enumerable/LINQ find helpers over dense CLR collections do not reproduce sparse holes or JavaScript callback semantics.

tests.name: holes are visited
tests.input: let n=0; const r=Array(2).find((v,i)=>{n++; return i===1}); console.log(n,r===undefined);

tests.name: deleting a future element still leaves an index visit with undefined
tests.input: const a=[1,2,3]; const seen=[]; a.find((v,i)=>{seen.push(String(v)); if(i===0){delete a[1];a.push(4);} return false}); console.log(seen.join('|'));
